source.title: MOSS-Audio-Tokenizer: Scaling Audio Tokenizers for Future Audio Foundation Models
source.authors: Yi-Tian Gong; Kuang-Wei Chen; Zhao-Ye Fei; Xiaogui Yang; Ke Chen; Yang Wang; Kexin Huang; Ming-Shu Chen; Rui-Xiao Li; Qingyuan Cheng; Shi-Min Li; Xi-Peng Qiu

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports audio-tokenizer reconstruction scaling, but does not test language-model held-out cross-entropy power laws, extrapolation from smaller runs, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. It cites language-model scaling work as background.
record.gate_note: The paper's own scaling experiments measure audio reconstruction metrics as model size and training batch size change. Those are related to scaling, but do not measure the claim's power-law loss behavior or compute-optimal split.
record.test_reason: The paper runs its own scaling sweeps on an audio tokenizer: parameters 319M–1169M (Fig. 5) and batch size 2^0–2^8 (Fig. 6). It reports these only as plotted trends in reconstruction metrics (SIM, STOI, PESQ). It fits no power law, reports no held-out loss or exponents, and makes no extrapolation or compute-optimal analysis. Its results therefore cannot show whether the power-law form (V1/V5) holds. It is more than citation-only, because it has its own scaling analysis that it calls stable and predictable, but it does not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that CAT reconstruction quality improves with model capacity and batch size, and call the batch-size scaling stable and predictable. They also stress that parameter count and quantization depth must be scaled together, because bitrate becomes the bottleneck. 'Predictable' is asserted qualitatively, with no fitted law.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales an end-to-end audio tokenizer and measures reconstruction metrics; it does not use the original language-model loss measurements or fitting procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Reconstruction quality varies with model parameter count, bitrate, and training batch size.

fits_no_version.finding: CAT reconstruction quality rises with parameter count, but smaller models saturate early. At low bitrates the 1169M model can underperform smaller models run at higher bitrates, so bitrate becomes the bottleneck.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Audio-tokenizer reconstruction gains from parameter scaling are capped by quantization capacity (bitrate), so both must be scaled together.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger batch sizes at fixed steps give better reconstruction on all speech metrics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For this audio tokenizer, more training throughput at fixed steps monotonically improves reconstruction fidelity.

fits_no_version.finding: End-to-end optimization keeps improving over 500k steps, while partial (frozen encoder/quantizer) optimization plateaus early (Fig. 4, Section 5.1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Whether an audio tokenizer keeps improving with training depends on jointly optimizing all components.

record.problems: The scaling evidence is presented as plots and qualitative trends, without reported fitted exponents or uncertainty estimates. The measured outcomes are audio reconstruction metrics rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version results were reported beyond the related audio reconstruction scaling trends recorded in r1–r2.

untested.parts: All: no language-model held-out loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
All: no fits extrapolated to larger runs.
All: the size sweep varies hidden dimension only, with no fixed-parameter shape comparison.
Whether a power-law form holds for audio tokenizers. Only monotone reconstruction-quality trends are shown, with no fitted form.
All: TTS and ASR downstream results are not related to tokenizer scale or loss.
All: no fitted exponents to compare.

record.verdict_notes: I changed the relation from cites_only to discusses because the paper has its own scaling section. It is still not a test, because no power-law fits or loss values are reported. Kaplan et al. [28] and Henighan et al. [29] are cited only as inspiration.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy versus parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power-law fits on smaller runs.
Loss-minimizing parameter and token allocation at fixed compute.
Architecture-shape comparisons at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same power-law form holds in audio or other modalities; the study reports reconstruction trends, not power-law fits.
Predictability of downstream-task performance from pretraining loss or scale.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocation on setup and fitting choices.

rows.subject: CAT parameter-scaling sweep
rows.operation_detail: Varied hidden dimension and model parameter count while keeping the quantizer at 32 layers and 12.5 Hz.
rows.value: figure only; the paper states that higher parameter counts improve reconstruction quality, while smaller versions saturate earlier
rows.note: The text summarizes the sweep across model sizes; the plotted metrics are audio reconstruction measures, not held-out language-model cross-entropy or power-law fits.
rows.check: Link and state are correct. The measure is audio reconstruction quality across bitrates from figures only, with no power-law fit, so it cannot bear on V1 or V5's power-law form. The text also notes smaller models saturate early and bitrate becomes the bottleneck.

rows.subject: CAT batch-size scaling sweep
rows.operation_detail: Varied global training batch size from a baseline factor of 2^0 to 2^8 while keeping training steps and other hyperparameters constant.
rows.value: figure only; the paper states that larger batch sizes yield better reconstruction fidelity across all evaluated speech metrics
rows.note: The reported trend is for audio reconstruction quality; the paper does not fit a power law or assess held-out cross-entropy.
rows.check: Link and state are correct. The batch-size sweep holds steps fixed and is shown as a figure only. It gives no loss and no fitted functional form.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
